Hi Ramya, thanks for the effort to document this.

However, I feel there are other approaches that are less complex and more directly available to those building OpenBMC images. Specifically, Yocto's `runqemu` script handles much of the magic of invoking qemu with the right arguments for the image build at hand:

https://docs.yoctoproject.org/dev/dev-manual/qemu.html

As a concrete use-case, I already use the `runqemu` integration to test all the kernel recipe bumps before I push them to gerrit.

Broadly, building an OpenBMC image tends to build the native qemu package with it, which `runqemu` invokes. The qemu recipe generally points at upstream qemu releases, and as such, so long as the necessary functionality is upstream, this should do the job.

As the person who maintains openbmc/qemu, the necessary functionality tends to be upstream. This is true for several reasons:

1. We maintain openbmc/qemu in the same way as we maintain openbmc/linux - all contributions must first go upstream, and may be backported if necessary
2. Where patches are in openbmc/qemu master but not in upstream's master branch, it's the case that they're instead queued for upstreaming in the ASPEED maintainer's branch[[1]](https://gitlab.com/qemu-project/qemu/-/blob/05f36f7c0512c40a8f929e8ba2ca3c825198f234/MAINTAINERS#L1214-L1234)[[2]](https://github.com/legoater/qemu/branches)
3. 2 is the case because my method of maintaining openbmc/qemu master is to rebase the patches in Cédric's branch back down to the most recent upstream tag.
4. The AST2500 and AST2600 have been around for quite a few years now, and much of the common functionality has already been modeled in qemu. It tends to be rare to hit something that isn't niche but also isn't modeled, and where that's the case, the patches to add support should be sent upstream.

From there, we just need the necessary variable configuration for `runqemu` to launch OpenBMC images. This is provided for ASPEED SoCs with e.g. [[3]](https://github.com/openbmc/openbmc/blob/19f42bb9dc8084ba5c8db61650d699f6de474c06/meta-aspeed/conf/machine/include/ast2600.inc#L17-L19).

I'll leave comments inline outlining equivalent `runqemu` invocations where possible.

The script above, copying the image file, and invoking the script as outlined here can largely be replaced with the following invocation of the `runqemu` wrapper provided by Yocto:

```
runqemu slirp snapshot nographic
```

Where it's necessary to directly pass through options to qemu, runqemu's `qemuparams=` argument can be used.

I'd rather we discussed this instead, with whatever tweaks are necessary to appropriately configure the network.
